 Live Updates: Iran says Strait of Hormuz reopening, seven-day ceasefire conditions still on the table
 By
 Frank Andrews , 
 Frank Andrews 
 Frank Andrews is a CBS News journalist based in London.
 Read Full Bio 
 Frank Andrews , 
 Duarte Dias 
 Duarte Dias 
 Digital Journalist 
 Duarte Pita Dias is based in CBS News' London bureau, where he works across digital platforms and for TV broadcasts.
 Read Full Bio 
 Duarte Dias 
 Updated on: October 18, 2026 / 3:02 PM EDT 
 / CBS News
 Add CBS News on Google 
 What to know about the Iran war today:
 Iran's foreign minister said Sunday the Strait of Hormuz would reopen within days if the U.S. complies with the conditions set out in the seven-day ceasefire proposal presented in September, which called for an end to the American naval blockade, lifting sanctions on Iranian oil and a ceasefire on all fronts.
 The U.K. Maritime Trade Operations monitoring agency said at least 10 vessels have been attacked in or near the Strait of Hormuz since last Sunday, a weekly high since war broke out in February, and 23 attacks were recorded since the start of the month, almost double the average.
 Yemen's foreign minister blasted Iran's offer to mediate the war between the internationally recognized government and the Iran-backed Houthi militant group. "When Iran's foreign minister and his officials offer 'mediation' in Yemen, they are offering to mediate a war ignited by the coup of the Houthi terrorist militia with their regime's backing," she said.
 New Updates
 3:02 PM / October 18, 2026
 Saudi-led military coalition and Houthis trade strikes amid intensifying conflict
 Conflict raged between the Houthis and the Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Iran-backed rebel group on Sunday, as both sides traded strikes. 
 In Riyadh, where intensifying violence has disrupted life for residents, the landmark Kingdom Centre skyscraper ordered "mandatory" remote working for office tenants until further notice. Although a reason for the order wasn't provided, it followed a security alert and two drone interceptions around the capital city, in addition to a number of attacks by Houthis on Saudi targets in recent weeks.
 Meanwhile, the Saudi-led coalition, which backs the internationally-recognized government in war-wracked Yemen, has launched repeated air raids on regions of the country that Houthis control. One alleged Saudi airstrike in northern Yemen  killed at least nine people and wounded 16 others on Sunday, the Houthis' Saba news agency reported.
 The coalition said Sunday that two pilots were killed when their helicopter crashed in Najran, near the Yemen border, blaming a "technical malfunction" for the incident. The Houthis said they "downed an Apache helicopter belonging to the Saudi enemy" in the same area.
 CBS/AFP

 2:43 PM / October 18, 2026
 Netanyahu says partnership with Trump will help "eliminate Iranian threat"
 Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu praised President Trump in multiple social media posts on Sunday, saying his relationship with the U.S. president will help "eliminate the Iranian threat." His comments came after Mr. Trump endorsed Netanyahu as the Israeli leader seeks reelection in a tight race.
 In a video released by his Likud party, Netanyahu called on voters to heed Mr. Trump's words, assuring them "we have crushed Iran" and adding that their partnership "will continue in order to eliminate the Iranian threat over the next two years, or even sooner."
 Netanyahu also said "Israel has never had a greater friend in the White House" than Mr. Trump, thanking him for his "clarity, courage and unwavering support" as the prime minister vowed to work with the U.S. to "never let Iran's regime get nuclear weapons."
 CBS/AFP

 link copied 
 1:38 PM / October 18, 2026
 6 injured by Houthi strike in southern Saudi Arabia, officials say
 Six people in southern Saudi Arabia were injured in a Houthi strike on Sunday, the Saudi Arabian civil defense agency said. The projectile struck a residential section of Najran, a city near the border with Yemen, according to the agency.
 "On Sunday, civil defence in the city of Najran responded to the fall of an enemy projectile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia at a residential site, resulting in six citizens being injured and material damage to three homes and three vehicles," the civil defense said on X .
 For weeks, the Iran-backed Houthis have targeted airports and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia on a near-daily basis as fighting between the kingdom and the rebel group has sharply escalated.
 CBS/AFP

 11:34 AM / October 18, 2026
 Trump endorses Netanyahu ahead of Israeli elections
 President Trump on Sunday endorsed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for reelection, saying on social media that he "has been a Great Warrior Prime Minister, and an even greater Partner for Peace in combatting the Islamic Republic of Iran."
 This is a coveted boost for Netanyahu because of Mr. Trump's popularity but one that the U.S. leader withheld for months as their strategies in the Middle East diverged.
 Netanyahu's government, the most nationalist and far-right in Israel's history, faces domestic criticism over security failures and international criticism over the treatment of Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza. Some of the government's senior officials are settlers themselves.
 "Bibi Netanyahu has been Strong, Brave, and Brilliant in the face of tremendous opposition, including that coming from even Israel, itself. Despite all of that, he has endured and, in fact, he has thrived!" Mr. Trump wrote on Truth Social.
 Netanyahu, on X , thanked Mr. Trump for his "tremendous support and the joint work."
 "Together we will complete the mission!" he added.
 Israelis are set to vote Oct. 27, in the first national elections since the 2023 Hamas attack on Israel.
 CBS/AP

 7:06 AM / October 18, 2026
 Iran says Hormuz reopening conditions still in place
 Iran's Foreign Affairs Minister said Sunday that Tehran's conditions to reopen the Strait of Hormuz still remain in place.
 Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency on Sunday that Tehran is still reviewing "comments" from the U.S. on the Iranian seven-day ceasefire proposal presented in September, but that the conditions to reopen the strategic waterway were still in place.
 "If they comply with our conditions, the Strait of Hormuz will reopen on the sixth day, and negotiations will begin on the seventh day," Araghchi said, referring to the seven-day timeline proposed by Iran which calls for the U.S. to lift its blockade on Iranian ports in order to resume negotiations and reopen the waterway. 
 "Our conditions are fair, and if the United States is willing to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, it can meet them within a few days," Araghchi added.
 By
 Duarte Dias

 5:45 AM / October 18, 2026
 Iran's new defense minister threatens "enormous damage" if U.S. resumes attacks
 Iran's newly appointed defense minister Mehrdad Akhlaghi threatened to inflict "enormous damage" on the United States and its allies in the Middle East if Washington resumes its military campaign against the country.
 "People can rest assured that they will most likely not dare to attack us," Akhlaghi told reporters shortly after securing the vote of confidence. "If (the U.S.) do, they themselves and the region will suffer enormous damage."
 CBS/AFP

 4:48 AM / October 18, 2026
 Office workers at Riyadh skyscraper told to stay home
 Office workers in the Kingdom Center skyscraper in Saudi Arabia's capital have been advised to work remotely "until further notice," amidst repeated attacks by the Iran-backed Houthi rebels on the country.
 "Kindly refrain from attending the offices during this period," the office management said in an email to tenants seen by Agence France-Presse news agency. 
 At a height of 992 feet and 99 storeys, the Kingdom Center skyscraper is an icon of Riyadh's skyline. The mall at the foot of the building remains open.
 CBS/AFP

 4:01 AM / October 18, 2026
 Tug boat struck near Strait of Hormuz
 A tug boat traveling near the Strait of Hormuz was struck by two unknown projectiles, a British maritime monitoring agency said Sunday.
 The U.K. Maritime Trade Operations said in a statement that a tugboat travelling southbound off the coast of the United Arab Emirates "reported being struck by 2 unknown projectiles."
 "The tug has sustained damage but is continuing on its route," the agency said, "one minor casualty has been reported."
 By
 Duarte Dias

 3:02 AM / October 18, 2026
 Saudi military says two pilots killed in helicopter crash near Yemen border
 The Saudi military said Sunday two pilots were killed when their helicopter crashed near the border with Yemen.
 "An AH-6i reconnaissance helicopter belonging to the national guard crashed and was destroyed in Saudi territory in the Najran area as a result of a technical malfunction, resulting in the death of its crew of two officers," coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki said, according to the official Saudi Press Agency.
 Saudi Arabia is currently engaged in a war with Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen, who have attacked major oil and airport infrastructure.
 CBS/AFP

 Updated 7:28 PM / October 17, 2026
 Saudi military intercepts 2 ballistic missiles, official says
 Residents in the Saudi capital of Riyadh received a mobile phone alert early Sunday morning local time warning of a "hostile aerial threat," Agence France-Presse journalists reported, after days of attacks from Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi militants.
 "Warning. The area is under a hostile aerial threat. Please remain calm, stay indoors or in a safe place away from windows and doors," read the alert, which was lifted a few minutes later.
 Col. Turki Al-Maliki, a spokesperson for a Saudi-led military coalition that supports Yemen's internationally-recognized government, later posted on X that Saudi Arabia had intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles that were fired by the Houthis toward the city of Khamis Mushait in southwest Saudi Arabia, as well as a drone that was fired at Riyadh. 
 CBS/AFP 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-strait-of-hormuz-yemen-houthis-saudi-arabia/#post-update-d5b8497c 
 link copied 
 2:46 PM / October 17, 2026
 Yemeni foreign minister criticizes Iranian offer to mediate Houthi war
 Yemen's foreign minister is blasting Iran's offer to mediate the war between the internationally recognized government and the Iran-backed Houthi militant group.
 "When Iran's foreign minister and his officials offer 'mediation' in Yemen, they are offering to mediate a war ignited by the coup of the Houthi terrorist militia with their regime's backing, and prolonged by that regime's arming, financing, and training of the militia and its supply of missiles, drones, and experts," Yemeni Foreign Minister Afrah Alzouba said as part of a lengthy statement . 
 "Tehran has made itself a party to the war on Yemenis," she continued. "Instead of offering mediation, its regime should withdraw its hand and its weapons from Yemen, respect the sovereignty of states, and abide by international law and the principles of good neighborliness."
 Iran's foreign ministry on Friday rejected Saudi Arabia's accusation that Tehran was involved in Houthi attacks on the kingdom, offering to mediate between the two sides.
 The Houthis are backed financially and militarily by Iran, officials from the U.S. and Israel, as well as many regional analysts, have said for years .
 "The Houthis are the most powerful proxy within the Iranian network, hands down," Mohammed Al-Basha, founder of the Basha Report, a U.S.-based risk advisory group, told CBS News. "Any U.S. military strategy planning a campaign on Iran will have to take into consideration what the Houthis will do next."
 By
 Mark Osborne 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-strait-of-hormuz-yemen-houthis-saudi-arabia/#post-update-85aad273

 1:57 PM / October 17, 2026
 Iranian foreign minister meets with several Middle East counterparts at regional gathering
 Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, one of the leading members of past negotiations with the United States, met with a handful of his counterparts on Saturday at a gathering of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation in Baghdad.
 Among those he met was Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan even as Turkey is part of a trilateral cooperation agreement with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, which is coming under fire from the Iran-backed Houthi militia.
 The two sides discussed "the latest developments in Palestine and Yemen, emphasizing diplomatic efforts to reduce tensions," according to the Iranian government.
 "During the bilateral talks, FM Araghchi also reviewed the latest developments in the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz, briefing his Turkish counterpart on ongoing diplomatic trends and emphasizing Islamic cooperation to face shared regional challenges," the Iranian government said on X .
 Araghchi also met with foreign leaders from Egypt, which said Saturday it would defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks; Libya; Lebanon; and Algeria.
 By
 Mark Osborne 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-strait-of-hormuz-yemen-houthis-saudi-arabia/#post-update-24ec3926

 11:41 AM / October 17, 2026
 Saudi strikes on Yemen kill 12, Iran-backed Houthis say
 Saudi strikes that began overnight have killed at least 12 people in Yemen, three of them children, Houthi media reported on Saturday.
 Saudi warplanes targeted "civilian homes" in Taiz governorate on Saturday, killing nine people and wounding 16, the Iran-backed group's news agency said, adding people were still trapped under the rubble.
 The agency had earlier reported overnight strikes in Dhamar province that killed three children and wounded 17 other people.
 It said the strikes were carried out "using cluster bombs, which are banned internationally."
 The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis has launched daily raids in Yemen backing the internationally recognized government in the country's long-running civil war.
 By
 AFP 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-strait-of-hormuz-yemen-houthis-saudi-arabia/#post-update-4a5b0787 
 link copied 
 11:02 AM / October 17, 2026
 Saudis intercept 4 drones over country in recent hours
 The Saudi-led coalition fighting against the Iran-backed Houthis have intercepted four drones over Saudi territory in the last few hours, the group said.
 The drones were intercepted over the capital city of Riyadh, and in the Eastern, and Southern regions, according to the coalition.
 The Houthis have regularly launched drones and missiles at the Saudis every day for the last several weeks. 
 The coalition announced overnight it had taken out two missile-launch platforms in the Saada Governorate, which is the northern-most region in Yemen and controlled by the Houthis. A missile launch one week ago hit King Khallid International Airport in Riyadh and killed 13 people.
 By
 Mark Osborne 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-strait-of-hormuz-yemen-houthis-saudi-arabia/#post-update-0769e039 
 link copied 
 10:37 AM / October 17, 2026
 President Sisi says Egypt ready to defend Saudi Arabia "if requested"
 Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi on Saturday said Egypt was ready to defend Saudi Arabia "if requested," as fighting flares between the kingdom and Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen.
 Since Yemen's war reignited in July, the Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi targets, including energy facilities and Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, where 13 people were killed in a single attack last Saturday.
 The Houthis have also blockaded the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to Saudi-flagged tankers, piling pressure on energy exports as Iran presses its own blockade on the Strait of Hormuz.
 Speaking at a graduation ceremony at the Egyptian military academy, Sisi said Egypt was "not looking for a role to play" in regional conflicts, but added it was "inconceivable" for Cairo to stand by while Saudi Arabia was "harmed or its security and stability threatened."
 "Egypt, of course, with the directives of His Majesty King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, will carry out any measure to protect you or defend you," he said.
 He added any deployment would require parliamentary approval and said he hoped lawmakers would convene in an emergency session to grant authorization "if it is requested of us."
 "I'm not talking about fighting anyone or attacking anyone," Sisi said. "We are speaking only about defense."
 By
 AFP 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-strait-of-hormuz-yemen-houthis-saudi-arabia/#post-update-029cd33e 
 link copied 
 10:12 AM / October 17, 2026
 Yemen's Houthis free 159 pro-government fighters under amnesty
 Yemen's Houthis on Saturday announced the release of 159 pro-government fighters under an amnesty announced after they seized swathes of land in a major offensive last month.
 The prisoners had "voluntarily surrendered themselves without fighting" as the Iran-backed group captured strategic positions along the Red Sea, Houthi official Abdelqader al-Murtada told a press conference in Sanaa.
 The Houthis' war with the Saudi-backed, internationally recognized government reignited in July after four years of calm, triggering attacks on Saudi oil shipments and other targets including airports.
 The International Committee of the Red Cross confirmed the unilateral release of 159 prisoners and said it had given support by organizing interviews and health checks, contacting families and helping arrange transport.
 Murtada said 323 prisoners were released under the amnesty last month after surrendering in Hodeidah governorate.
 By
 AFP 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-strait-of-hormuz-yemen-houthis-saudi-arabia/#post-update-b13d8220 
 link copied 
 9:49 AM / October 17, 2026
 Iran backs "political process" to resolve Saudi-Houthi conflict, foreign minister says
 Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Saturday that Tehran supports a "political process" to resolve the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis.
 The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi targets, including energy facilities and Riyadh's international airport, where 13 people were killed in a major attack one week ago.
 "We support an inclusive and comprehensive political process as the only practical and sustainable way to resolve the issue," Araghchi said in a speech at the Organization of Islamic Cooperation in Baghdad.
 Araghchi repeated Iran's offer to mediate between the two sides. Deputy Foreign Minister Saeed Khatibzadeh previously said Riyadh has not responded to Iran's overture.
 On Friday, Iran denied having anything to do with the Houthi attacks, after Saudi Arabia accused Tehran of encouraging the group's escalation.
 In his speech, Araghchi also said "either we build security together, or we will endure insecurity together," adding Tehran was willing "to cooperate with all its brothers and neighbours to achieve the first option."
 The Houthis in Yemen and Hezbollah in Lebanon are part of Iran's "Axis of Resistance" against Israel and the United States, which also includes armed groups in Iraq.
 By
 AFP 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-strait-of-hormuz-yemen-houthis-saudi-arabia/#post-update-aa2089ae 
 link copied 
 5:31 AM / October 17, 2026
 Oil tanker reportedly hits mine in Strait of Hormuz
 Iran's Revolutionary Guards Corps on Saturday said an oil tanker was on fire in the Strait of Hormuz after hitting a mine in the waterway at the heart of the Middle East war.
 "A supertanker in violation of regulations, carrying more than two million barrels of crude oil and attempting to pass illegally through the Strait of Hormuz, struck a mine, triggering an explosion and a fierce fire," the Iranian military said.
 The statement did not specify the exact location of the incident.
 "The tanker attempted to cross the strait with U.S. support... by deactivating all its tracking systems," the Guards added, also posting a video of a vessel in flames during the night.
 By
 AFP 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-strait-of-hormuz-yemen-houthis-saudi-arabia/#post-update-4525e9fc 
 link copied 
 4:47 AM / October 17, 2026
 Ship attacked by RPG fired from small boat, British maritime agency said
 The U.K. Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) monitoring agency reported on Saturday a second attack on a ship off the coast of Saudi Arabia, which took place a day early.
 In a post on social media , the UKMTO said: "The master of a tanker has reported being attacked by an RPG (rocket-propelled grenade) from a small boat, resulting in damage to the aft port quarter."
 Friday's attack is the second reported by the agency on that day off the coast of Al Jubayl in Saudi Arabia.
 "Crew are accounted for and reported safe," the UKMTO said, but the full extent of the damage and environmental impact were not known at the time of the report.
 By
 Duarte Dias 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-strait-of-hormuz-yemen-houthis-saudi-arabia/#post-update-498112ed 
 link copied 
 3:01 AM / October 17, 2026
 Ship struck by "unknown projectile" off the coast of Saudi Arabia, maritime agency says
 A British maritime agency said Saturday it had received a report of a vessel struck on the Persian Gulf on Friday.
 The U.K. Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said the tanker had been struck by an "unknown projectile" off the coast of Saudi Arabia.
 "All crew are reported safe and have been evacuated. There is no reported environmental impact at the time of report," the statement added.
 The UKMTO had previously reported that October had become the busiest month for reported attacks on ships in the Strait Hormuz.
 By
 Duarte Dias 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-strait-of-hormuz-yemen-houthis-saudi-arabia/#post-update-01464e7e 
 link copied 
 9:56 PM / October 16, 2026
 Reported shipping attacks jump in Strait of Hormuz, British monitor says
 A British monitor says October has become the busiest month for reported attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz since March, during the Iran war's opening months.
 That's as the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said it was "struggling to accurately report" the true number of attacks since most ships now refuse to report them.
 Still, UKMTO said 10 attacks were reported in the week ending Friday. One ship sank. Since early July, most attacks have occurred off Oman, where the U.S. military has been guiding vessels at risk of Iranian attack.
 There has been an uptick in attacks since President Trump late last month rejected a Tehran proposal to end the war and open the strait, though indirect negotiations have continued.
 By
 The Associated Press 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-strait-of-hormuz-yemen-houthis-saudi-arabia/#post-update-34f05e70 
 link copied 
 4:12 PM / October 16, 2026
 2 missiles strike airport in Yemen's port city of Aden, officials say
 Two missiles struck the airport in Yemen's port city of Aden on Friday night, police said, blaming Iran-backed Houthi rebels for the second such attack in less than a week.
 Police said no casualties were reported as fighting escalates in the latest front in the Iran war, one in which the rebels have attacked both neighboring Saudi Arabia and Yemen's internationally recognized government that's backed by the kingdom. 
 A security official and a traffic controller told The Associated Press an area of the Aden airport that hosts a military unit aligned with the Saudi-backed government was hit. Both spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak to the media.
 There was no immediate claim of responsibility.
 By
 The Associated Press 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-strait-of-hormuz-yemen-houthis-saudi-arabia/#post-update-a2aa862e 
 link copied 
 2:26 PM / October 16, 2026
 Iran denies Saudi accusation of involvement in Houthi attacks
 Iran's foreign ministry on Friday rejected Saudi Arabia's accusation that Tehran was involved in Houthi attacks on the kingdom, offering to mediate between the two sides.
 "The Islamic Republic of Iran rejects any claim that Iran has played a role in Yemeni (Houthi) operations," Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said in a statement, reiterating Tehran's offer to act as a bridge between the Houthis and Riyadh.
 Regardless of how involved Iran has been in Houthi attacks, the two groups have long held close ties . 
 They were once a relatively marginal group within what Iran calls its Axis of Resistance — a loose alliance of anti-Israel, anti-U.S. militant groups that includes Hamas in Gaza and Hezbollah in Lebanon.
 "The Houthis are the most powerful proxy within the Iranian network, hands down," said Mohammed Al-Basha, founder of the Basha Report, a U.S.-based risk advisory group. "Any U.S. military strategy planning a campaign on Iran will have to take into consideration what the Houthis will do next."
 Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia have killed about 20 people in the last several weeks, including 13 in one strike on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport last weekend.
 CBS/AFP 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-strait-of-hormuz-yemen-houthis-saudi-arabia/#post-update-5b844456 
 link copied 
 12:47 PM / October 16, 2026
 Iran's president denies nuclear ambitions, says country ready for talks
 Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian denied Friday that Tehran sought nuclear weapons, expressed readiness for dialogue and condemned U.S. sanctions during talks with Georgia's prime minister.
 In his meeting with Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze, Pezeshkian also called for closer ties with Georgia, weeks after Tbilisi cut aviation links between the two countries following U.S. sanctions targeting Iranian airlines.
 The two met on the sidelines of a U.N. biodiversity summit in Armenia's capital, Yerevan.
 "Iran is not seeking nuclear weapons, and we consider the malicious propaganda against our country to be lies," Pezeshkian said, according to a statement from his office.
 "We have always been ready for dialogue. They think they can force us to surrender, but we will not bow to coercion," he added, calling U.S. sanctions against Tehran "unjustifiable and inhumane."
 Georgia's Civil Aviation Agency said in September it would comply with U.S. sanctions, while Kobakhidze insisted Tbilisi was not imposing its own bilateral sanctions on Tehran.
 Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian attends a meeting of the Commonwealth of Independent States in Turkmenbashi, Turkmenistan, Oct. 9, 2026, in this pool photograph distributed by the Russian state agency Sputnik. 
 Sergei Bobylyov/Pool/AFP via Getty Images
 By
 AFP 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-strait-of-hormuz-yemen-houthis-saudi-arabia/#post-update-3d7e665c 
 link copied 
 12:11 PM / October 16, 2026
 Saudi-hosted Asian Cup soccer tournament remains on schedule despite Houthi attacks
 Asian Cup organizers insisted Friday the continental soccer championship set to be held in Saudi Arabia in early 2027 remains on track despite a wave of missile and drone attacks on the host country in recent days.
 The Saudi organizing committee issued a statement Friday saying it is continuing to coordinate closely with the Asian Football Confederation. The tournament is scheduled for Jan. 7 to Feb. 5.
 "Preparations across all organizational and operational areas are progressing according to the approved schedule, including work on venues, facilities and supporting services," Saudi organizers said. "The focus remains on delivering a world-class tournament experience for participating teams, fans and media from across Asia, while bringing the continent together through football."
 South Korea's Professional Footballers' Association had earlier expressed concerns following a series of attacks on the Asian Cup host country by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels.
 "The continued military tensions and security instability in the Middle East are issues that can never be taken lightly," Lee Keun-ho, head of the South Korean player union, said in a statement. "The safety of our national team, as well as all players participating in the Asian Cup, is a serious concern."
 At least 19 people, including foreigners, have been killed in more than a week of Houthi attacks targeting the Riyadh international airport, the headquarters of Saudi oil giant Aramco and other aviation, oil and military facilities across the kingdom.
 Several sporting events have already been canceled or postponed in Saudi Arabia, including Netflix's Six Kings Slam tennis tournament; women's tennis' WTA Finals, which were moved to the U.S.; multiple matches for the Saudi soccer club Al-Nassr, which features Cristiano Ronaldo; and an Olympic qualifying event for BMX cycling.
 AP/CBS 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-strait-of-hormuz-yemen-houthis-saudi-arabia/#post-update-4730e6d9 
 link copied

 Attacks on Yemen government palace compound killed 5, officials say
 Attacks on the palace compound of Yemen's internationally recognized government Thursday killed at least five people and wounded more than a dozen others, government officials said.
 In a Facebook post late Thursday, Health Minister Qasem Buhaibeh said security guards and other employees at Maashiq palace in Yemen's southern port city of Aden were among the casualties.
 Aden has been the seat of Yemen's government since 2015. The Houthis claimed responsibility for the attacks, saying they targeted a military operations headquarters associated with Saudi forces backing the government.
 Two of the missiles launched by the Houthis on Thursday struck near the headquarters of the Saudi-backed coalition forces in Aden, causing damage, a Yemeni government official said.
 The official, speaking on condition of anonymity because he wasn't authorized to speak to the media, said Friday the missiles landed near the compound used by the coalition in Buraiqah, a neighborhood west of the palace. No senior officials were there at the time of the attack, he said.

 Iraq says Iran war has deprived it of $60 billion in oil export revenue
 Iraq has lost around $60 billion during the U.S.-Iran war, Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said Thursday, as the fighting has blocked or severely impeded a waterway crucial to its oil exports.
 OPEC member Iraq was producing about 4 million barrels of oil per day (bpd) before the conflict, and exporting about 3.5 million bpd – mostly carried by tankers out of the Persian Gulf via the Strait of Hormuz.
 Iran's ongoing threat to vessels that fail to seek its permission to transit the strait has forced Iraq, which lacks sufficient storage capacity, to halt most production and fall back on limited exports via Syria and Turkey, by truck and pipeline respectively. Syria is set to provide an overland oil route to bypass the strait , the head of Syrian Petroleum Co. said last week.
 "Iraq has suffered losses estimated at around $60 billion during the recent war between the United States and the Islamic Republic of Iran," Hussein told his Italian counterpart in Rome, according to a statement from the Iraqi foreign ministry.
 After a heavy drop in production, Iraqi oil exports, which provide about 90% of the country's revenues, recovered modestly last month, reaching 2.6 million barrels per day between Sept. 1 and 21, according to the oil ministry. But at the same time, Iraq's foreign currency reserves have shrunk by $20 billion and consumer prices have risen sharply, plunging it into economic crisis.

 Norwegian teen sentenced in U.K. to 20 years in prison for plotting murder for Iran-linked gang
 A Norwegian teenager convicted of traveling to Britain to carry out a contract killing on behalf of an international crime gang linked to Iran was sentenced Friday to 20 years in prison.
 Johannes Kongsnes Natland, 19, was found guilty in July of conspiracy to murder for agreeing to shoot someone unknown to him for $28,000 last year. He was arrested at a hotel in Huddersfield, in northern England, with two guns and ammunition two days after arriving in the U.K.
 In bodycam video released by police from the early hours of March 19, 2025, Natland emerges topless from his room and mimes a shooting gesture at a firearms officer before being slammed against a wall.
 It remains unknown who his intended target would have been.
 Natland, who was working part time at a pizza restaurant at the time of his arrest, was recruited by a Swedish organized crime group known as the Foxtrot Network while he was playing a game online. The group has links to the Iranian government, according to London's counterterrorism police unit.
 Natland was hired by a 17-year-old known as "Generalen." A court in Norway last year convicted the teenager of attempting to "contribute to murder" and sentenced him to 14 years in custody. A 16-year-old is awaiting trial in Norway for his role in the conspiracy.

 White House prepares plans to use weapon dubbed "mother of all bombs" on Iran, sources say
 The White House and Pentagon have prepared plans to use a Massive Ordnance Air Blast bomb to hit military sites in Iran if ordered by President Trump, sources familiar with the matter told CBS News.
 A Pentagon official told CBS News: "The Department of War plans for a wide range of operational scenarios to execute Presidential and Secretary level direction and to ensure mission success in any operational environment."
 A White House spokesperson said: "We do not comment on sensitive military plans that may or may not exist. President Trump keeps all options on the table to ensure that Iran can never have a nuclear weapon."
 Last week, Mr. Trump said the U.S. would not attack Iran before the midterm elections. He also touted "productive conversations" with Iran, though he did not provide specifics.
 CNN first reported Thursday on the plans to use the Massive Ordnance Air Blast Bomb, or MOAB, on Iran.
 Mr. Trump set a precedent for using the MOAB, also known as the "mother of all bombs," when it was used in 2017 to attack an Islamic State cave complex in Afghanistan. The bomb is the largest U.S. non-nuclear weapon, weighing upwards of 30,000 pounds at a cost of $170,000 per unit.
